emergency.seoTitle: Urgent Dental Care in Cheonan: Pain & Swelling | Seoul BD Dental
emergency.description: Sudden tooth pain, swelling or injury? Identify medical warning signs, understand the role of initial dental care and know why follow-up treatment matters.
emergency.heroQuestion: When something suddenly hurts or breaks, what needs attention first?
emergency.story: Severe tooth pain, a swollen face or an injured tooth can make it hard to think clearly. You may worry about being unable to explain the problem or about having to agree to major treatment immediately. The first task is to judge urgency and reach the right care setting; definitive treatment may follow after the immediate risk is assessed.

patientQuestions.question: Should I wait if swelling makes swallowing difficult?
patientQuestions.answer: No. Seek immediate emergency medical help rather than waiting for a routine dental response.

patientQuestions.question: Can everything be finished at the first visit?
patientQuestions.answer: Not always. Safety and initial treatment come first, with later stages explained separately.

patientQuestions.question: If painkillers help, can I cancel the review?
patientQuestions.answer: Pain relief does not prove the underlying problem has resolved. Follow the agreed care plan.

tradeoff.gain: Urgent assessment can identify immediate risks and connect initial care with definitive treatment.
tradeoff.burden: The first visit may not complete all treatment and symptoms can change.
tradeoff.decision: Choose the appropriate care setting first, then clarify the remaining stages.

sections.title: Recognise when to seek emergency medical help
paragraphs: Difficulty breathing or swallowing, rapidly spreading swelling or serious facial injury can require immediate emergency medical care. Do not wait for a routine dental booking or an online reply in these circumstances. Tell the receiving team the main symptoms, when they started and any relevant medicines or medical conditions.

sections.title: For an injured tooth, identify what happened
paragraphs: A tooth knocked out, chipped or moved out of position needs prompt assessment. Baby teeth and permanent teeth require different responses: do not replant a knocked-out baby tooth. Avoid handling a knocked-out permanent tooth by the root or letting it dry out while arranging urgent professional advice. Do not delay seeking care while trying to perfect a home solution.

sections.title: Separate first aid from completion of treatment
paragraphs: An urgent visit may address pain, infection, bleeding or injury without completing every root canal or restoration stage. Ask what was treated, what remains and when to return. Pain relief or antibiotics do not necessarily remove the source of infection. New or worsening symptoms may need earlier care than the planned review.

benefits: Prompt assessment can prioritise infection, injury or bleeding concerns.
A clear follow-up plan helps prevent symptom relief from becoming an unintended treatment stop.
limits: Initial relief cannot guarantee that the tooth is preserved or the infection fully resolved.
Delayed follow-up can leave the underlying source untreated.
care: Provide the symptom timeline, injury details, medication list and relevant medical history.
Follow the return instructions and seek urgent help for breathing or swallowing difficulty or rapidly worsening swelling.

faq.question: Are antibiotics enough for a dental abscess?
faq.answer: They do not necessarily remove the source. Appropriate dental treatment and reassessment may still be needed.

faq.question: Should a knocked-out baby tooth be put back?
faq.answer: No. Do not replant it; arrange prompt assessment of the child and injury.

faq.question: What if a temporary filling comes out after urgent care?
faq.answer: Contact the treating team for advice about protection and the next appointment rather than leaving the tooth open indefinitely.

faq.question: Does an urgent appointment guarantee immediate availability?
faq.answer: No. Confirm actual appointment arrangements; emergency warning signs should be directed to emergency medical care without waiting.
